items.title: Human CYP1A2 metabolism of organophosphorus pesticides and nerve agent surrogates
items.abstract_or_text: CYP1A2 contributes 13-15% of hepatic CYP450 content and plays a critical role in the metabolism of approximately 10% of pharmaceutical drugs in the human body. CYP1A2 has been previously reported to bioactivate and detoxify both the thion (P=S) and oxon (P=O) forms of organophosphorus (OP) compounds. In this study, we determined the capacity of CYP1A2 to degrade OP compounds using LC-MS/MS, as well as the inhibition of its activity by OP compounds using the previously developed pFluor50 assay. CYP1A2 was selective in metabolizing thions over oxons, and several OP compounds inhibited its activity in a time- and dose-dependent manner. To further investigate the mechanism of CYP1A2-OP interactions, molecular docking studies were performed using a crystal structure of CYP1A2 (PDB ID: 2HI4). Linear correlation analysis between CYP1A2 inhibition at 10 M with 30 minute preincubation and the % OP compound remaining at 2 hours (R = -0.71, P<0.001) showed a moderate but significant correlation. Based on these findings, CYP1A2 was identified as a potential bioscavenger for OP compound metabolism, supporting the future integration of experimental and in silico data for developing artificial intelligence (AI) / machine learning (ML) models for prediction of CYP1A2-mediated metabolism of existing and emerging OP compounds, including those of toxicological and chemical warfare relevance.

items.title: Vision Transformers as a Framework for Imaging Fluorescence Correlation Spectroscopy
items.abstract_or_text: Fluorescence correlation spectroscopy (FCS) is widely used for quantifying molecular dynamics in live cells. However, conventional FCS relies on the autocorrelation function (ACF), a lossy transformation that discards higher-order information, mathematically couples distinct biophysical parameters, and requires long measurements (~50,000 frames, or ~1 minute) that obscure short-lived transient events. To overcome this information bottleneck, we introduce ImFCSViT, a spatiotemporal Vision Transformer-based framework that bypasses the ACF representation entirely, operating directly on raw fluorescence image stacks. By introducing a dedicated normalization token to preserve global intensity statistics, our approach simultaneously extracts four biophysical parameters (diffusion coefficient D, particle density N, particle brightness B, and PSF structure factor {sigma}0) in a single forward pass. Requiring only 2.5 s of data, and potentially down to 1 s (a 1-2 order reduction in data requirement), our approach accurately recovers diffusion coefficients while utilizing its spatial field-of-view to reveal spatially heterogeneous, slow-diffusing sub-populations in lipid bilayers and live-cell plasma membranes that are invisible to classical FCS. By leveraging the data-driven representational learning capabilities of deep learning, we present a flexible, generalizable, and powerful tool for mapping complex, multi-parameter spatiotemporal dynamics in biological systems.

items.title: Signature Recontextualization: Mapping perturbational signatures across biological contexts
items.abstract_or_text: Perturbational transcriptomics is a powerful tool for understanding gene function and drug effects, yet predicting how perturbations manifest across different biological contexts remains a central challenge, limiting translation from model systems to clinically relevant tissues. Despite growing interest in this problem, benchmarking efforts have been hindered by inconsistent evaluation tasks, heterogeneous metrics, and limited assessment across perturbation types and biological systems. Here, we introduce a benchmarking framework for cross-context perturbation-signature prediction (a task we define as signature recontextualization), grounded in explicit definitions of the prediction task, target-data availability, and evaluation metrics centered on signature recovery. The framework evaluates prediction performance across three target-context data regimes: (1) control only, where only control profiles from the target context are measured; (2) low coverage, where a limited subset of perturbations in the target context are measured; and (3) high coverage, where most perturbations in the target context are measured. This design enables systematic assessment of how prediction performance depends on target-context sample size while providing a standardized basis for comparing methods. We evaluate newly developed projection-based (projectCor) and network-based (netProp) methods alongside deep learning-based foundation models (scGPT, STACK) and statistical baselines. The benchmark spans diverse perturbational datasets: CRISPR knockdowns and drug perturbations in cell lines, plus in vivo chemical perturbations in rat tissues from DrugMatrix, extending evaluation beyond isolated cell-line models to tissue-level responses. For each method, evaluation was limited to the datasets, and perturbation types each model supports. Across tasks, projection and network propagation approaches show strong flexibility across perturbation types and biological contexts, and in several cases match or exceed the performance of deep learning and foundation models. We further show that perturbation predictability varies substantially with pathway conservation, transcriptional response strength, and baseline similarity between source and target contexts. All datasets, methods, and evaluation utilities are released as an open-source R package (sigRecon), providing a foundation for reproducible benchmarking and future method development.

items.title: Extracellular Vesicles Derived from L-MYC Neural Stem Cells Mediate Neuroprotection in 3D Models of Chemotherapy- and Radiation-Induced Neurotoxicity
items.abstract_or_text: Background/Objectives: Cancer survivors frequently experience long-term neurocognitive impairments following chemotherapy and cranial irradiation, yet experimental models that enable mechanistic investigation of therapy-induced neurotoxicity at the transcriptional level remain limited. This study aimed to develop a human three-dimensional (3D) neural tissue model derived from L-Myc immortalized neural stem cells (LMNSCs) and use transcriptomic profiling to identify molecular pathways underlying chemotherapy- and radiation-induced neural injury and extracellular vesicle (EV)-mediated recovery. Methods: LMNSCs were differentiated in a 3D, methylcellulose-based culture to generate neural tissue containing neurons, astrocytes, and oligodendrocytes. Cultures were exposed to methotrexate (MTX) or ionizing radiation to induce neural injury and subsequently treated with LMNSC-derived EVs. Neural injury and repair mechanisms were evaluated by immunocytochemistry and bulk transcriptomics. Results: MTX and irradiation induced dose-dependent injury, exhibited by loss of neuronal complexity and reduced glial populations. LMNSC-EV treatment promoted recovery of neuronal and glial populations following MTX- and irradiation-induced injury. Transcriptomic analysis of irradiated cultures revealed activation of inflammation, DNA damage, and stress-response pathways, which were attenuated after treatment with LMNSC-EVs. Conclusions: LMNSC-based 3D neural tissue provides a human-relevant platform for modeling cancer therapy-induced neurotoxicity. Furthermore, LMNSC-EVs represent a promising cell-free regenerative therapeutic that restores injury-associated inflammatory, stress, and metabol-ic transcriptional programs after radiation-induced neural injury.

items.title: PYTHIA, a transferable machine learning framework for simultaneous defect and adsorption site optimization
items.abstract_or_text: Machine learning has permeated material optimization, providing high value. Nevertheless, its re- liance on a high number of samples limits its applicability to relatively explored material families. In this paper we extend the applicability of machine learning to novel and understudied materials through the PYTHIA (Probabilistic Yet Transferable Hierarchical Interaction Architecture) framework. Pythia utilizes two of the most powerful machine learning concepts, foundational models and transfer learning. We employ a complex foundational model trained on a large dataset of chemically similar molecules, on a target that is physically close to our prediction target. Then, we freeze the weights and perform subspace alignment with the use of a transformer layer and add uncertainty quantification with gaussian processes. These two layers can be trained on a limited dataset yet allow us to leverage the gained knowl- edge and the studied materials and complex architectures. items.title: Single-cell analysis of West Nile virus infection in brain organoids identified a serine synthesis enzyme as a determinant of viral neural tropism and a druggable antiviral target
items.abstract_or_text: The cellular and molecular determinants of human neuroinvasive West Nile virus (WNV) disease are currently poorly defined. Previous studies of WNV neural infection relied on rodent models and immortalised cell lines that diverge from human brain tissue. Herein, we established a reproducible human cerebral organoid model of WNV infection and profiled it by virus-inclusive single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-Seq) to obtain an understanding of WNV-host interactions in the context of human neural tissue. We found that WNV showed preferential tropism to progenitor cells, immature neurons, and astrocytes, while the mature neurons were largely resistant to infection. Astrocytes were identified as the principal source of interferon (IFN) and the main hub of IFN-signalling, whereas mature neurons expressed little viral RNA-sensing machinery or STAT1 and responded weakly to infection and to IFN. The differential gene expression analysis between WNV-permissive and nonpermissive cells demonstrated that virus-susceptible cells had high baseline expression of the serine synthesis and one-carbon metabolism genes PHGDH, SHMT2, and MTHFD2, which were not induced by infection. RNA-interference and pharmacological inhibition of phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase (PHGDH) restricted WNV replication, confirming the requirement of this gene for WNV infection. In addition, the FDA-approved drug disulfiram, known to inhibit PHGDH, also reduced viral replication in neural progenitors and cerebral organoids. Overall, these results provide the first comprehensive single-cell-level characterisation of WNV neural infection in human neural tissue. They identify de novo serine synthesis as a metabolic dependency of WNV in human neural cells that can be targeted as a host-directed antiviral therapy.

items.title: Sequence architecture of RNA reveals key molecular signatures driving RNA phase separation
items.abstract_or_text: Biomolecular condensates are dynamic membraneless assemblies that organize various cellular processes through liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS). RNA is an active regulator of biomolecular condensates and influence their formation through sequence-encoded features. Despite its established role in condensate formation, no computational framework exists to identify underlying signatures to predict LLPS-associated RNAs. We develop an interpretable hybrid framework to distinguish reviewed, experimentally supported LLPS-associated RNAs from background RNAs. We uncover biologically meaningful sequence properties associated with condensate participation. Each RNA is represented by 167 handcrafted descriptors capturing composition, k-mer usage, sequence complexity, repeat organization and dinucleotide autocorrelation together with 640-dimensional contextual embeddings from RNA-FM. These representations are integrated through cross-validated stacking with neural-network meta-learner. The framework achieves an AUC-ROC of 0.935, AUC-PR of 0.944 and MCC of 0.782. Feature statistics, ablation analysis and SHAP interpretation reveal a distributed sequence architecture dominated by altered local k-mer usage with additional contributions from low-complexity burden, repeat-associated organization and long-range dinucleotide pattern. Biological case studies including MALAT1 and TMPO-AS1 further connect these patterns with experimentally characterized modes of multivalent RNA-protein assembly. Together, the results show how interpretable machine learning can move beyond prediction to identify sequence features that generate mechanistic hypotheses for RNA-mediated condensation.

items.title: VERA: A Responsible AI Dashboard for Assessing LLM Deployments in Light of the EU AI Act
items.abstract_or_text: Institutions that deploy large language models in regulated settings often need technical evidence of responsible AI practices before approving a deployment. COMPL-AI provides a technical interpretation of the EU AI Act that organises this evidence under six principle groups and eighteen technical requirements, twelve of which current benchmarks can measure. The benchmark suites that produce this evidence are typically operated from a command line, while the staff who approve deployments are non-engineers. We present VERA, an open-source self-hosted dashboard deployed to facilitate responsible AI processes within a large European bank. A reviewer selects a model and runs public benchmarks against it. VERA scores the twelve requirements that current benchmarks can measure and instruments the energy consumed by each evaluation, adding run-level evidence for environmental impact. We run four served open-weight models through the requirement pipeline, and the dashboard displays a score for each measurable requirement. A within-subject study then compares how participants read these benchmark results: from the raw output files in one condition, and through the VERA dashboard in the other. The dashboard reduced the time needed to perform the responsible AI assessment, reducing the time required from 56 seconds using raw files to 30 seconds using our dashboard, on average. Our dashboard scored highly (4.36 out of 5) on usefulness in the survey conducted within the organization. The dashboard and the study material are released publicly to promote replicability and reproducibility in different organisational contexts.

items.title: AgentTriage: Replayable Security Diagnosis Across Heterogeneous Agent Runtimes
items.abstract_or_text: When tool-use agents write files, execute code, or send data, their final responses do not explain the resulting security events, and heterogeneous runtimes expose the relevant evidence through incompatible interfaces. We present AgentTriage, an executable contract for replayable security diagnosis across heterogeneous runtimes. The contract admits conclusions whose claims cite canonical runtime events and requires abstention when mandatory evidence is missing. Runtime overlays normalize native observations, while a deterministic pipeline joins invocation and result lifecycles, constructs a typed provenance graph, selects a policy-decisive slice, and binds claims to recorded evidence. Given the same normalized trace, overlay version, and pre-run policy oracle, the diagnosis can be recomputed and its claims re-checked without language-model judgment. Across five runtimes, one contract captures all 159 applicable executions, with an audit of native and synthesized identifiers. On 120 adjudicated cases, AgentTriage achieves 0.858 grounded joint diagnosis, 0.966 required-evidence coverage, and a 0.036 unsupported-claim rate, improving joint diagnosis by 0.175 (95% CI [0.092, 0.258]) over the strongest same-schema baseline. These results quantify the precision of replayable diagnosis and the observation boundaries that require abstention. We release an open-source implementation and selected sanitized evidence at https://github.com/AsnGs/agenttriage-open-source.

items.title: Multi-Peptide Prompting Enables In-Context Learning in Protein Language
items.abstract_or_text: Protein language models (PLMs) are trained primarily on individual protein sequences, yet many peptide-discovery problems require inference from only a small number of labeled examples. Here, we show that single-sequence PLMs can perform in-context peptide learning without gradient updates, task-specific retraining, or architectural modification. We introduce multi-peptide example prompts (MPEPs), in which demonstration peptides are concatenated with glycine spacers and used as context for scoring query peptides by their prompted probability. We evaluate this approach across a synthetic pattern-completion task, secondary-structure classification, and MHC-II binder prediction using both encoder-only ESM-2 models and decoder-only ProGen2 models. Across tasks, performance improves with the number of peptide examples and with model scale, indicating that PLMs can extract shared sequence-level properties from prompted examples. We further introduce a difference score that contrasts positive-example and negative-example MPEPs, reducing compositional biases in raw PLM probabilities and substantially improving classification. On MHC-II binder prediction, MPEP-based classification with larger ESM-2 models matches or exceeds low-data classifiers trained on frozen ESM-2 embeddings, while requiring no training. These results reveal an unexpected in-context inference capability in single-sequence PLMs and establish MPEP conditioning as a lightweight strategy for low-data peptide classification.

items.title: Beyond Watching and Searching: Benchmarking Agents for Video-centered Deep Research Reports
items.abstract_or_text: Deep research agents synthesize open-web evidence into long reports, but current benchmarks do not evaluate research centered on a source video. We introduce Video-Centered Deep Research Report Generation. Given a video and user request, an agent identifies research questions, retrieves external multimodal evidence, and produces an interactive report linked to relevant video moments. This task has direct practical value because it helps users locate relevant moments, verify claims, reproduce demonstrated procedures, and make informed decisions from video content. We present a skill-based workflow and OmniDR-Bench for this task. For evaluation, we propose Omni Atomic Rubric Trees (Omni-ARTs). Each tree contains three dimensions, 23 shared directions, and task-specific atomic binary criteria. The directions test audiovisual grounding, multimodal evidence use, and interactive presentation. Audited Rubric Construction (ARC) builds these trees through independent evidence collection, automated checks, behavioral calibration, and iterative human review. OmniDR-Bench contains 50 Chinese and English tasks across 19 realworld subcategories. It includes 6,414 criteria. Across 18 agent configurations, the best system scores 63.3 out of 100. Current agents still need broader content coverage, stronger causal and logical analysis across modalities, and more accurate citation support. We further analyze models, harnesses, skill configurations, video categories, and research trajectories. The code and data are released at https://github.com/marinero4972/OmniDR-Bench.

items.title: Synthetic-to-Real Code-Switched ASR: A Spontaneous Nepali-English Podcast Benchmark
items.abstract_or_text: Nepali-English code-switched conversational speech presents severe challenges for automatic speech recognition (ASR), chiefly through script confusion (inappropriate mixing of Devanagari and Latin orthography) and elevated error rates at language switch points. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) can adapt multilingual foundation models, but human code-switched audio is expensive to collect and annotate. We curate a new benchmark of 13,044 spontaneous podcast utterances (15.45 h total; 10,214 test, 2,830 dev), audited and verified to eliminate machine translation leakages and acoustic loops. We investigate a two-stage synthetic-to-real adaptation framework: Stage 1 applies SFT on 0.95 h of speech synthesized via a multi-speaker, dual-engine TTS pipeline; Stage 2 explores Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with transcription and script rewards. We find that synthetic SFT provides the primary cross-domain transfer to spontaneous human speech, reducing Mixed Error Rate (MER) from 23.40% to 21.52% (-1.88 pp) and switch-point error rate (SPER) from 35.89% to 28.77% (-7.12 pp). Subsequent GRPO yields small, statistically significant adjustments on 173 test utterances (1.69%), driving English script confusion (SCR_en) from 6.45% to 6.36% (p <= 0.001) and SPER to 28.70% (p = 0.022 clustered). Crucially, ablation reveals that in this SFT-converged encoder-decoder setting, an auxiliary script reward term yields performance identical to MER-only optimization because rollout candidate groups exhibit near-zero script variance on synthetic data. On monolingual benchmarks, SFT improves Nepali MER by 2.71 pp (stabilizing at 18.42% after GRPO, a 2.38 pp gain over baseline) while preserving English lexical WER (3.38% vs. 3.33%). Verified transcripts, timestamps, episode metadata, and reconstruction scripts are publicly released.

items.title: A Physics-Informed Fourier Neural Operator Framework for Zero-Plating Fast Charging of Lithium-Ion Batteries via Real-Time Electrochemical State Estimation and Barrier-Riding Optimal Control
items.abstract_or_text: Extreme fast charging of lithium-ion batteries is critically limited by internal lithium plating at the negative electrode-separator interface, driving rapid degradation and thermal hazards. Real-time mitigation is fundamentally impeded because the interfacial plating overpotential (ηplating) is inaccessible to non-invasive sensors, leaving conventional protocols blind to metallic lithium deposition. While high-fidelity Doyle–Fuller–Newman (DFN) models resolve these dynamics, their computational cost (∼ 8 s) precludes embedded closed-loop control, whereas empirical equivalent circuit models lack the spatial resolution to detect plating. To resolve this trade-off, we develop a physics-informed 1D Fourier Neural Operator (FNO-1D) surrogate incorporating an explicit cumulative charge integral Q(t) = ∫ I dt to preserve mass conservation. Trained on 7,771 continuum DFN trajectories, the surrogate achieves a 4, 349× speedup (1.84 ms inference) with high fidelity (V RMSE = 5.40 mV, η plating , RMSE = 2.24 mV). Coupled with an Ensemble Smoother with Multiple Data Assimilation (ESMDA), the framework filters sensor noise (±10 mV to 5.94 mV) and reconstructs unobservable plating dynamics (RMSE = 4.12 mV, 95% CI = ±3.22 mV), establishing continuous closed-loop observability. A Barrier-Riding Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC) policy then maximizes charging current along the degradation boundary. Across a 10% - 80% SOC window, it cuts charging time by 21.7% (33.7 min vs. 43.0 min CC-CV)while strictly preventing lithium plating (η plating ≥ +14.81 mV > +5.0 mV), limiting peak temperature to 38.5◦C, and decreasing SEI growth by 21.5%. Finally, transferability is experimentally validated across two phys ical cycler benchmarks: cross-chemistry transfer on Oxford pouch cells, and chemistry-matched validation on commercial RWTH Aachen Sanyo 18650 NMCcells, achieving a terminal voltage tracking RMSE of 33.02 mV (86.0% error reduction over zero-shot transfer) providing an experimentally grounded paradigm for degradation-free fast charging.

items.title: Agent K: An Agent-Orchestrated Pipeline for Mapping Genes to Biosynthetic Pathway towards Metabolite Discovery
items.abstract_or_text: The identification of biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) and their associated metabolic path- ways is central to genome-guided natural product discovery. However, existing computational tools depend on fragmented workflows for data processing, annotation, and analysis, which re- quire substantial manual intervention and lack seamless integration across heterogeneous plat- forms and tools. Here, we present, Agent K, an agent-orchestrated framework that automates the end-to-end process from bacterial whole genome sequence analysis to biosynthetic pathway mapping and metabolite discovery as candidate gene products for functional insights. The sys- tem employs a large-language-model (LLM) agent to coordinate multiple bioinformatics tools, enabling dynamic execution, data integration, result interpretation, and flexible and intuitive visualization. By integrating genomic sequences to functional annotations and pathway-level reconstructions, the framework facilitates the identification of candidate gene products, their biosynthetic pathways associated with individual BGCs, and the putative metabolites produced by those pathways. The developed novel agentic framework provides a user-friendly scalable and extensible solution for automated high-throughput analysis and mapping of bacterial secondary metabolism pathways for interactive exploration of candidate potential.

items.title: Learning Robot Behavior Priors from Non-Robotic Synthetic Data
items.abstract_or_text: Real robot data, rich across tasks and morphologies, is often treated as the bottleneck for training robot learning models, including embodied foundation models that aim for zero-shot physical transfer. In this paper, we investigate the degree to which such models can acquire necessary structure using data from systems without embodiment. To this end, we test if inexpensive, procedurally generated synthetic data can yield useful priors before a model observes any real-world behavior. We study this through robot action prediction, a natural pretraining objective and a direct test of whether structure learned from arbitrary synthetic tasks transfers to embodied settings. We introduce three data generation pipelines that model mathematical abstractions of robotic control, and use them as pretraining priors for a Transformer. We demonstrate that a model trained purely on this non-robotic data attains non-trivial zero-shot prediction performance on unseen physical robot tasks via an in-context learning mechanism, and that our specialized control priors notably improve upon generic causal priors. We also compare against a compute-matched baseline trained on real robot data, and find that it outperforms our model but only on the datasets it was trained on. These findings suggest that procedurally generated, mathematical abstractions can yield useful robotic priors, offering a potential complement to expensive embodied data collection.

items.title: Building Presentation Intelligence for High-Quality Slide Generation
items.abstract_or_text: PowerPoint presentations (PPTs) are a dominant medium for communication across diverse domains, yet high-quality PPT generation still depends heavily on labor-intensive human effort. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) for agentic tasks have created both new opportunities and challenges (Chen et al., 2026) for automatic PPT generation. In this work, we present a unified training framework for automatic PPT generation toward presentation intelligence, integrating cross-validated data synthesis, guided teacher enhancement, and verifiable reward optimization. We first construct a cross-validated pipeline for data synthesis, with explicit control over both difficulty and validity. We then develop a teacher-enhancement framework grounded in rules and prior knowledge to substantially strengthen the instructional capacity of teacher models. Building on this, we further improve supervised fine-tuning (SFT) through a mixed-teacher strategy and a lightweight outcome-driven trajectory filtering method. Finally, based on the resulting SFT models, we introduce a suite of verifiable aesthetic metrics together with a GRPO-based reinforcement learning framework to optimize slide-level visual attributes beyond text-only supervision. Experiments show that our enhanced SFT pipeline improves Qwen-3.6-27B and Qwen-3.6-35B-A3B by 7.45 and 9.35 points on PresentBench, respectively, surpassing GLM-5.2 while maintaining strong generalization. Reinforcement learning further improves performance across five aesthetic dimensions, compensating for the limitations of SFT in visual refinement. Overall, the results demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework for high-quality PPT generation.

items.title: The ModelSEED Biochemistry Database, 2026 update: grading multi-source thermodynamics
items.abstract_or_text: The ModelSEED Biochemistry Database (https://modelseed.org/biochem) supplies foundational mass- and charge-balanced reaction networks for metabolic reconstructions. Here we present an update on the biochemistry where the database has been expanded to [~] 46,000 compounds, and [~] 56,000 reactions, featuring [~] 37,000 metabolic structures. We have expanded our approach for handling thermodynamic data, enabling multiple sources of data to be derived, integrated, and presented to the wider research community. We now publish predictions of pKa, reaction energy (and respective uncertainties), and estimates of reaction direction from multiple independent sources. Each reaction is graded gold, silver or bronze according to the strength of the evidence behind it, so that users can weigh its reliability directly. We also release reaction directions predicted by an ensemble of large language models. This multi-source approach exposes agreements and discrepancies between sources for [~] 33,000 reactions. Finally, to ensure data integrity, a new conflict-resolution pipeline reconciles structures across sources, documenting input from curators. Our work is publicly available at https://github.com/ModelSEED/ModelSEEDDatabase.

items.title: Do protein representations encode variant function? Diagnosing residue-level protein attributions via embedding-space gradients
items.abstract_or_text: A common workflow in protein engineering involves building fitness predictors on protein language models (pLMs) to estimate a variant's fitness and interpret which residues drive it. Attribution methods such as integrated gradients address this second goal by assigning residues contributions to the variant's predicted fitness. However, without ground truth for residue importance, it is unclear whether these attributions reflect what the predictor learned about function. Here, we introduce IGLOO, a framework that scores residue-level attributions against synthetic fitness landscapes with known per-residue importance. Across experimental axes, high predictive accuracy did not guarantee faithful attributions. We identify model interventions that more than double attribution skill scores and raise TOPSIS by 29%, with similar patterns holding in real -amylase and {beta}-lactamase datasets. IGLOO provides a protocol for probing what pLMs learn and a guide for choosing defaults when using residue attributions to pick sequence edits and build more trustworthy protein models.

items.title: Active Learning framework for Antibody Binding Affinity Prediction
items.abstract_or_text: Antibody engineering campaigns must prioritise variants from large combinatorial libraries under limited assay budgets. We present a Gaussian process (GP) active-learning benchmark for antibody-antigen binding affinity prediction across eight public AbBiBench assays spanning influenza hemagglutinin antibodies CR6261 and CR9114 and AAYL-series scFv libraries against the SARS-CoV-2 Spike HR2 peptide. The framework embeds variable heavy and light (VH/VL) sequences with ESM-2 650M, trains GP surrogates over compressed protein-language-model representations, and evaluates kernel, acquisition, representation, classical featurisation, and labelling-budget choices under a unified budget of 10\% of each full pool with a label-blind seed and a fixed held-out evaluation split. Across the benchmark, Tanimoto+UCB has the highest mean Recall@2\% point estimate among tested kernel-acquisition configurations, achieving 57.8\% mean Recall@2\% across five random seeds (68.3\% when scored against the acquisition-eligible pool), compared with 9.6\% for random selection -- a gap that is significant by a paired Wilcoxon test across datasets (p=0.0078); its point estimate is not significantly different from RQ+UCB or Tanimoto+EI at five seeds. We adopt the continuous Tanimoto kernel of gessner2024. The same configuration recovers the largest fractions of top binders in the influenza libraries (74.2\% on 3gbn\_h1, 82.7\% on 3gbn\_h9, and 84.9\% on 4fqi\_h3) while exposing harder AAYL combinatorial landscapes where recall remains lower and more variable. An additional three-seed representation ablation, run under the original protocol and not repeated after the evaluation corrections, ranked ESM-2 650M highest (mean Recall@2\% 0.673 \pm 0.28) among ProtBert, AntiBERTy, AbLang2, ProGen2, and classical encodings. On BindingGYM, the same configuration matches or exceeds ALLM-Ab on two of three datasets using the 100-sample held-out test metric. Structure-mapped Integrated Gradients and KernelSHAP analyses recover CDR-region attribution patterns consistent with contact-derived paratope geometry, though threshold-free (AUROC) analysis shows this qualitative agreement is not matched by strong residue-level discrimination. These results support Tanimoto-kernel GP active learning as a simple, reproducible strategy for label-efficient antibody affinity optimisation with qualitative structural validation.

items.title: UNDERSTANDING THE ROLE OF AROMATICITY IN TAUTOMERIC EQUILIBRIA
items.abstract_or_text: Tautomerism, the interconversion of small molecules via proton and π-electron shifts, poses a fundamental challenge in drug discovery, as different tautomers can exhibit distinct physicochemical properties and receptor-binding profiles, while computational approaches have been widely applied to predict tautomeric equilibria, most methods often overlook electronic properties such as aromaticity, which are critical to molecular stability. Here, we explore the role of aromaticity in tautomeric equilibria using a computational framework that integrates density functional theory (DFT) calculations with interpretable machine learning (ML) models. Aromaticity, which is challenging to measure experimentally, is quantified via Harmonics Oscillator Model of Aromaticity (HOMA) values and incorporated as a molecular descriptor. To enhance interpretability, we employ shallow ML models and assess feature contributions both intrinsically and using post-hoc explainability techniques. Our results demonstrate that both intrinsic and post hoc feature importance approaches capture similar trends associated with aromaticity. This highlights the complex influence of aromaticity on tautomeric equilibria and suggest that ML models, when combined with quantum-mechanics-based descriptors and explainable feature analyses, could be applied more broadly to capture important trends in other physicochemical properties beyond tautomer stability.

items.title: Flexible force field-based screening and machine learning predictions for CO2 sorption and diffusion in MOFs
items.abstract_or_text: Machine learning offers an efficient route for screening metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), but most existing models rely on rigid-framework simulations that neglect framework flexibility. In this work, DFT-derived flexible force fields were used to calculate CO2 sorption and self-diffusion for 5,418 MOFs, providing the training data for machine-learning models capable of rapidly predicting these properties. We investigated different ML algorithms, featurization methods, and the role of physical descriptors in predicting CO2 sorption and self-diffusion in MOFs. For CO2 sorption, a categorical boosting classifier coupled with Stoichiometric-45 featurization method used with scalar descriptors provided predictive accuracy of 76.1%. For CO2 self-diffusion, we tuned a categorical boosting regressor on revised autocorrelation functions coupled with scalar descriptors and achieved moderate predictive accuracy (R2 = 0.69). These results demonstrate that machine learning trained on properties generated from flexible force field simulations can substantially accelerate computational screening while incorporating key effects of framework flexibility, providing an efficient strategy for discovering MOFs for low-pressure CO2 capture. Summary Computational screening of 5,418 metal–organic frameworks using flexible DFT-based force fields captures framework motion effects on CO2 sorption and self-diffusion. Machine learning models were evaluated across descriptors and algorithms. A CatBoost classifier achieved 76.1% sorption accuracy, while an autocorrelation-based regressor predicted self-diffusion (R2 = 0.69), demonstrating the value of flexibility-aware modeling.

items.title: Understanding the Relationship Between Synthetic Conditions and H 2 Uptake Capacity in Oxidatively Activated Turbostratic Carbons through Machine Learning
items.abstract_or_text: The relationship between synthesis parameters, porosity, and H 2 uptake in activated carbons is a field of significant investigation and discussion. Conclusions about these relationships are typically drawn from limited datasets of carbons produced for a given publication, and are not able to consider the interplay between various synthesis parameters and properties of the resultant turbostratic carbons. We present the first attempt at understanding the relationship between synthesis parameters and H 2 uptake capacity in turbostratic carbons, using the single point pore volume as a proxy due to the dearth of available high pressure H 2 isotherms. The methods used herein have exploited a dataset of 237 samples to determine the most important synthesis parameters in determining the porosity of the product and thus their suitability for high pressure H 2 storage applications.

items.title: Image-Charge Barriers, Not Polaron Kinetics, Limit Charge Extraction at Ligand-Passivated CsPbI3 Interfaces
items.abstract_or_text: Charge extraction across inorganic perovskite–organic ligand interfaces represents a critical materials bottleneck in perovskite optoelectronics, yet the defectindependent electrostatic origins of this process remain poorly understood. Here, we present a multiscale framework that combines first-principles density functional theory with macroscopic Scharfetter–Gummel drift-diffusion simulations to isolate and quantify this intrinsic transport barrier on CsPbI3 surfaces passivated by methylammonium (MA), butylammonium (BA), and phenethylammonium (PEA). items.title: Reactive Machine-Learned Potentials Improve Predictions of Water Diffusion Behaviour in Defective Industrial Zeolite HY
items.abstract_or_text: Dealuminated HY (USY) zeolites are of major industrial catalytic importance, and the defects they contain, such as extraframework aluminum (EFAL) and silanol groups, strongly influence the behaviour of adsorbed species. Here, we show that reactive neural network-based machine learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) provide a substantial improvement in the simulation of water diffusion in these catalysts. They yield markedly improved agreement with quasielastic neutron scattering (QENS) measurements of mobility for models of intact framework regions, refined further once EFAL and silanol defects are included explicitly, capturing the additional hindrance these sites impose on water motion. The ability of MLIPs to generate and stabilise realistic defect structures constitutes a step change in the molecular level and nanoscale modelling of industrial zeolites. This combined capability enables the quantitative investigation of defect-specific effects on nanoscale diffusion and provides a new approach for accurately modelling transport in industrially relevant zeolite catalysts.

items.title: Proton-Gated Cobalt Catalysis Redirects Persistent Sulfinyl Radical Coupling toward Enantioselective C–S Bond Formation
items.abstract_or_text: The enantioselective construction of aliphatic C(sp3)–S stereocenters from alkyl radicals remains challenging. Persistent sulfinyl radicals are attractive partners for radical cross-coupling. However, their rapid diffusioncontrolled coupling with transient alkyl radicals provides limited opportunity for stereochemical discrimination. Here, we report a dual photoredox/cobalt catalytic system in which a Brønsted acid acts as a critical mechanistic gate, redirecting persistent sulfinyl radical coupling from a direct PRE-dominated pathway toward cobaltcontrolled enantioselective C–S bond formation. Mechanistic studies support reduction of Co(II) to Co(I) and subsequent formation of a Co(III)–H species in the presence of HX. Hydrogen-atom transfer between Co(III)–H and the sulfinyl radical generates RSOH, which subsequently associates with a chiral cobalt species to organize the sulfur center for stereoselective radical capture. The use of aprotic alkyl radical precursors, including alkyl trifluoroborates and trialkylboranes, decouples radical generation from proton availability and reveals the critical role of the Brønsted acid in stereocontrol. This method accommodates diverse alkyl radical precursors and enables a practical alkene hydroboration–sulfinylation cascade for the synthesis of enantioenriched sulfoxides.

items.title: SABLE: Scalable Affine Bayesian Latent-space Exploration
items.abstract_or_text: Complex objects such as engineering designs and proteins are often difficult to optimise because their design spaces exhibit high-dimensional structure and objective evaluations are expensive. Generative models provide continuous latent representations, but their latent spaces can have thousands to tens of thousands of dimensions, creating a regime where the latent dimension D greatly exceeds the evaluation budget. We introduce SABLE, a Bayesian optimisation method for high-dimensional latent spaces with an isotropic distribution and limited budget. SABLE uses a Bayesian affine surrogate for prediction and acquisition, treating higher-order structure as surrogate discrepancy. After N observations, the slope update has dimension at most N-1, yielding a decomposition of each query into an in-span component optimised by expected improvement (EI) in at most N dimensions and an off-span component governed by a scalar norm. We show that the off-span norm implicitly selected by affine EI can lead to underexploration, and SABLE instead prescribes it using a finite-horizon schedule, without restricting search to a learned subspace. A recompression scheme reduces information to \mathcal O(M) pseudo-observations, bounding refitting cost by \mathcal O(M^2D+M^3) while keeping parameter inference, prediction, and acquisition decisions to tens of milliseconds. Across synthetic benchmarks and latent-space optimisation tasks, SABLE achieves high sample efficiency and reduces decision time by several orders of magnitude at large budgets.

items.title: Post-Hoc Feature Selection Layer for Neural Networks Interpretability
items.abstract_or_text: The interpretability of complex neural networks remains a critical challenge, especially for models already deployed in high-stakes domains. To address this, we adapted the Feature Selection Layer (FSL) to optimize feature weights post-training, a variant we term post-hoc FSL. Our approach reframes the FSL as a lightweight, trainable module that integrates with already frozen pre-trained models on tabular datasets to highlight the features the original model considers most important. This post-hoc FSL learns feature relevance by fine-tuning its weights based on the original model's learned outputs. Crucially, this process is non-invasive, operating without altering the original model's architecture or its learned parameters. We conducted our experiments using both statistical and visual metrics, including accuracy, F1 score, recall, precision, weighted t-SNE and silhouette score, and also analyzed the stability of the post-hoc FSL on high-dimensional synthetic and real-world tabular datasets. We compared the post-hoc FSL feature weighting method using these metrics against the original embedded FSL and other post-hoc interpretability methods, such as Integrated Gradients, Noise Tunnel, DeepLIFT, Gradient SHAP, and Feature Ablation. Experimental results demonstrate that the post-hoc FSL feature weighting method successfully identified relevant features across the different datasets, maintaining the predictive power of the original neural network while enhancing its interpretability.

items.title: Unconstrained learning of equivariant atomistic properties
items.abstract_or_text: Machine-learned interatomic potentials based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have made first-principles accuracy routine for the potential energy surface (PES). Their backbones, often O(3)-equivariant by design, are increasingly used to learn other atomistic properties. Many of these are of high angular order or pseudotensorial character, defined per atom, or expanded on large atom-centered basis sets. Such targets strain equivariant GNNs, whose tensor products grow steeply in cost with angular order and can fail to represent the target if truncated, forcing difficult trade-offs between hyperparameters. Unconstrained models like the Point-Edge Transformer (PET) instead replace explicit O(3) algebra with edge-to-edge attention and learn equivariance from data, so that the same backbone can in principle learn any equivariant property. We demonstrate how to use PET to learn molecular dipoles and polarizabilities, NMR chemical shielding tensors, and auxiliary-basis expansions of the electron density. Increasing the backbone size systematically improves both accuracy and equivariance error, and targeted architectural and training choices reduce the symmetry breaking further. PET matches or improves on the released reference models at lower inference cost and, compared with equivariant models, a smaller memory footprint. The predictions give accurate IR and Raman spectra and isotropic shieldings; the predicted densities accelerate self-consistent field calculations and give one-shot ground-state properties, and pretrained density models transfer to higher levels of theory by fine-tuning on little data. The impact of approximate equivariance is small for most observables, further validating this approach to train fast, accurate, and useful surrogate models for properties beyond the PES.

items.title: Is High Local Accuracy Enough? Geometric Consensus with Support-Adaptive Statistical Personalization for Federated Learning
items.abstract_or_text: Real-world deployment of personalized federated learning (PFL) requires adapting to heterogeneous clients while preserving recognition performance beyond local distributions. However, high local accuracy can conceal failures on locally rare or absent classes. Effective personalization should therefore strengthen global recognition while raising the personalization floor. We propose an evaluation protocol that complements local accuracy with global, rare-class, and unseen-class evaluations to reveal generalization obscured by local scores, and assesses personalization floors among the worst-performing clients to expose weaknesses hidden by aggregate performance. To meet these deployment challenges, we propose FedGRC, a unified PFL framework integrating generalization and personalization through (i) Consensus-Guided Representation Learning (CGRL), which learns discriminative representations through shared directional and magnitude guidance; (ii) Multilayer Metric Synthesis (MMS), which constructs a shared covariance metric from these multilayer representations for statistical classification; and (iii) Support-Adaptive Shrinkage Personalization (SASP), which adapts class means within this metric by shrinking local estimates toward shared means according to local sample support, enabling adaptation while retaining shared knowledge. Extensive experiments, including benchmarking against 21 methods across 5 heterogeneity settings on 3 datasets and comprehensive ablation studies, validate the effectiveness of FedGRC. On CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, FedGRC surpasses state-of-the-art (SOTA) baselines in global recognition and personalization floors by at least 2.17% and 2.13%, respectively. On the real-world heterogeneous FedRS dataset, it outperforms the respective best baselines by 2.15%, 3.30%, and 4.61% in local adaptation, global recognition, and the personalization floor.

items.title: Padding to k: A Minimum Count in the Schema Makes Open-Weight Models Pad Their Extraction Lists
items.abstract_or_text: Extraction pipelines ask language models for JSON that follows a schema, and the schema can set a minimum number of list entries. We ask what models do when the document holds fewer items than that minimum. Under a preregistered plan, we test eight open-weight models on 558 real documents from nine annotated datasets, with six more models on hosted services as a reference. Three findings stand out. First, models treat the count as a target: a minimum shown in the schema, but not enforced, raises the share of lists longer than the true count from 34.5% to 55.4%. Second, the padding is hard to catch, because most added entries are real text taken from the document; about half of them pass a check that each entry occurs in the source. Third, common fixes help only partly: a line saying fewer items are fine removes the effect on average but misses more true items, a count in prose ("up to k") also raises over-counting, an "N/A" option under an enforced minimum still leaves half the lists padded, and re-asking with the validation error makes padding far more common. We release the code, answer lists and run records at https://github.com/AbhishekBarali/padding-to-k

items.title: Vision Transformers for Estimating Irradiance Using Data Scarce Sky Images
items.abstract_or_text: Accurate estimation of diffuse horizontal irradiance (DHI) is critical for optimising photovoltaic system performance and energy forecasting yet remains challenging in regions lacking comprehensive ground-based instrumentation. Recent advancements using Vision Transformers (ViTs) trained on extensive sky image datasets have shown promise in replacing costly irradiance measurement equipment, but the scarcity of long-term, high-quality sky imagery significantly restricts practical implementation. Addressing this critical gap, this study proposes a novel dual-framework approach designed for data-scarce scenarios. First, calculated atmospheric parameters, including extraterrestrial irradiance and cyclic time encodings, are integrated to represent sky conditions without utilising any instrumentation. Next, a sequential pipeline initially predicts synthetic global horizontal irradiance (GHI) and uses it as a feature, to refine DHI estimation. Finally, a dual-parallel architecture simultaneously processes raw and overlay-enhanced fisheye sky images. Overlays are generated through unsupervised, physics-informed cloud segmentation to highlight dynamic sky features. Empirical validation is performed using data from the Chilbolton Observatory, chosen for its temperate climate and frequent cloud variability. To simulate data-scarce conditions, models are trained on a single month (e.g., January) and evaluated across a temporally disjoint, full-year test set. Under this setup, the sequential and dual-parallel frameworks achieve RMSE values within 2-3 W/m^2 and 1-6 W/m^2, respectively, of a state-of-the-art ViT trained on the complete dataset. By combining physics-informed modelling with unsupervised segmentation, the proposed method provides a scalable and cost-effective solution for DHI estimation, advancing solar resource assessment in data-constrained environments.

items.title: TwinStore: A Synthetic Consumer Platform Using Vision--Language Models
items.abstract_or_text: We present TwinStore, a source-available synthetic consumer platform for physical retail built on vision--language models. TwinStore turns a store into a digital twin---from 82 ready-made formats, a floor-plan image or phone photos of its shelves---and fills it with synthetic shoppers who plan a trip, walk the aisles and decide what to buy by looking at rendered shelves with packs, price tags and promotion signs. Every trip ends in a receipt, so a layout, price, pack or promotion can be tried on the same shoppers before it reaches the store. Around this core, TwinStore provides 3D playback, paired comparisons and layout optimization, shopper interviews, a trade-area model, counterfactual edits of real shelf photos, a marketing studio with eleven tools, and an assistant that turns a plain sentence into a drafted study or an answer grounded in a run's own numbers. In a held-out validation on eleven public datasets, simulated receipts approach the households' own natural variation (category-mix divergence 0.017--0.018 against a real drift of 0.012), price elasticities fall inside the range measured in the field, and three independent decision models agree. TwinStore runs on cloud or on-device models and is distributed with installers for Windows, macOS and Linux.

items.title: Population-scale drug target and variant prioritization with Varformer
items.abstract_or_text: Human genetic variation is a powerful driver of therapeutic target prioritization, yet current models struggle to aggregate variable numbers of variants per gene and are bottlenecked by the scarcity of validated targets. We present Varformer, a multimodal transformer that uses cross-modal attention to integrate contextual representations of missense variants with gene-level features. Trained via positive-unlabeled learning on clinically validated targets across four genetic ancestry groups, Varformer achieves a precision@20 of 0.95, 0.86, and 0.48 across three benchmarks of increasing difficulty. It surpasses a logistic regression ablation by 20% and DrugnomeAI by 23% on the hardest benchmark. Cross-population rank normalization isolates targets with consistent genetic support across ancestry groups. The variant encoder also scores individual variants. Across 1,164 carrier-variant pairs in Genes & Health, Varformer ranked the known pathogenic variant in the carrier's top 20 in 57% of pairs. Varformer is available as an open-source framework for unified target and variant prioritization.

items.title: VHH-Bench: A Benchmarking Framework for Evaluating Nanobody–Antigen Complex Predictions Across CDR3 Conformations
items.abstract_or_text: Accurate prediction of nanobody–antigen complex structures is critical for the development of diagnostic, therapeutic and biosensing applications. However, progress in this area have been constrained by the limited availability of experimentally determined nanobody–antigen complex structures. Recent advances in deep learning have enabled highly accurate prediction of protein structures and protein-protein complexes, yet accurate modelling of nanobody–antigen interactions remains challenging due to the diverse binding modes exhibited by nanobodies. Here, we present VHH‑Bench, a benchmarking workflow for the systematic evaluation of nanobody–antigen complex structure prediction methods. We curated a non-redundant dataset of experimentally resolved nanobody–antigen complexes and evaluated six state-of-the-art models: AlphaFold3, Boltz-2, Chai-1, ESMFold2, HelixFold3 and Protenix-v2. Complexes were stratified according to CDR3 conformation, enabling separate assessment of kinked and extended nanobody classes. Prediction performance varied substantially between models and conformational classes. Protenix-v2 achieved the highest overall docking accuracy, success rate and proportion of high-quality predictions, with its advantage most pronounced for nanobodies with extended CDR3 conformations. In contrast, all evaluated models showed reduced accuracy and higher failure rates for complexes containing kinked nanobodies. While increased stochastic sampling provided slight improvements in some cases, its overall impact was limited and did not substantially affect the relative performance ranking of the evaluated models. VHH-Bench provides an extensible and reproducible benchmarking workflow for standardised dataset curation, nanobody classification, model evaluation and confidence analysis, facilitating the rigorous assessment and future development of nanobody–antigen complex prediction methods. The VHH-Bench framework is available at https://github.com/haiboyugroup/VHH-Bench.

items.title: FAIRaman: making clinical Raman spectroscopy data FAIR through biobanking and NeXus standards
items.abstract_or_text: Raman spectroscopy is increasingly applied in biomedical and diagnostic research, generating spectral datasets that could support the development of robust artificial intelligence (AI) models for disease diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment guidance. However, most clinical Raman datasets remain difficult to reuse across laboratories because spectra are often stored separately from structured metadata describing the samples, their clinical context, experimental conditions, and data governance. This limits reproducibility, external validation, multicentre integration, and the development of transferable models. Here, we introduce FAIRaman, a FAIR-by-design framework and open-source software tool for the structured organisation of clinical Raman spectroscopy data. FAIRaman combines the hierarchical logic of the Investigation–Study–Assay (ISA) model with biobanking-derived descriptors for sample, donor, and processing-event annotation, and with NeXus/NXraman-inspired metadata for Raman acquisition parameters and spectral data. The resulting structure implemented in the open HDF5 file format. The software, developed in Python, converts native Renishaw WDF files and vendor-neutral text-based spectral files into FAIRaman-compliant HDF5 files through a graphical user interface (GUI), allowing users to combine batch-level metadata with sample-specific clinical data. We demonstrate the framework using a real Raman map of breast cancer tissue, and a Raman spectrum acquired from plasma-derived extracellular vesicles. These examples show that spectral data, acquisition metadata, and clinical sample descriptors can be stored within a single structured file and that the stored information can be easily retrieved using independent, freely available software tools.

items.title: Distribution Function Analysis of Crystalline and Low-Dimensional Materials
items.abstract_or_text: Atomic pair distribution function (PDF) analysis from X-ray total scattering is a powerful methodology for determining atomic structure and arrangements across crystalline, disordered, nanostructured, and low-dimensional materials on both laboratory and synchrotron instruments. Fundamentally, PDF analysis relies on two core pillars—PDF data reduction from one-dimensional (1D) total scattering profiles and real-space structural modeling—often accompanied in rapid-acquisition experiments by upstream two-dimensional (2D) detector image processing. However, conventional workflows remain fragmented across disconnected software tools, forcing researchers to manually combine multiple programs and preventing the simultaneous optimization of measurement reduction parameters and crystal structure parameters that is standard in X-ray Rietveld refinement. Furthermore, mainstream PDF modeling engines rely on legacy physical approximations: they enforce three-dimensional (3D) periodic boundary conditions (requiring artificial vacuum supercells for 2D nanosheets), treat atomic scattering factors as angle-independent constants (causing peak distortions in compounds with large atomic number contrast), and approximate number density baselines using macroscopic bulk volume assumptions. By bringing parameters outside the calculation engines rather than locking them inside built-in optimizers, this architecture allows multiple module instances across data reduction and structural modeling to be optimized simultaneously by modern optimization algorithms, machine learning libraries, and autonomous AI agents.
